done_when: The worker brief lets a worker update any existing test its intended change breaks, outside its scope, naming each changed test and why in its handoff; the review brief no longer reports such test files as outside scope but reports a test weakened to hide a real defect as a P1; tests through forge work and forge close show both

findings.body: The task-brief assertions check the permission and handoff phrases separately, but never check that an existing broken test may be changed outside Scope. Replacing the task-specific instruction with “You may also update an existing test your intended change breaks, but only inside Scope; name each such test and why it changed in your handoff” leaves both assertions passing while contradicting the required exception. Assert the permission, outside-Scope exception, and handoff requirement together in the task brief returned by `forge work`.
findings.title: Not done: forge work task-brief test enforces outside-Scope permission

findings.body: The new instruction asks the reviewer to check the worker's handoff, but `forge close` passes only the generated prompt and a fresh Git clone to review (`src/forge/review.py:145–182, 247–260`). Claude's output is kept in an uncommitted `.git/forge/` work log (`src/forge/repo.py:100–110`; `src/forge/worker.py:366–383`), and the Codex path records only a pending question from its final text (`src/forge/worker.py:165–168`). The reviewer therefore cannot verify whether each changed test was named and explained. Supply the handoff to review or remove this unverifiable check.
findings.title: Reviewer cannot inspect the worker handoff it is told to verify

why: Workers stop to ask before updating an existing test their intended change breaks, because the test file is outside the task's scope; it happened seven times on 2026-09-28
